theme: Excavation coverage, hidden settlement landscapes and archaeological survey design
question: Why do recorded and excavated Indus-site counts differ, what can area estimates and repeat surveys establish, and which overlooked settings warrant discriminating investigation?
outcome: A 12,362-word reviewed manuscript and 33-page PDF use 69 cited references from 72 source records, 50 local witnesses and 21 editorial regions. Historical 96/roughly 1,000 counts cannot form a current fraction with 142 Early and Mature excavations through 2024. Ganweriwala estimates of 81.5, 66.7 and approximately 33 ha have different spatial definitions. Local comparisons distinguish confirmed recording omissions, missing map associations, remote proposals and finer mound units. A source/effort concordance precedes a proposed 24-block preservation pilot; no national site or artifact total is fitted.
challenge: Counts and phase units differ; selected mound validation cannot identify regional recall. Aliases, historical-map filters, unreachable target horizons, landform chronology and context association constrain inference. Source supplements and historical inventory lineage remain unresolved. Initial P18 bounds, one area attribution, merged demotion rules and profile-level pilot wording needed correction. CLI authentication/path handling and DOI/diagram print layout required repairs.
remedy: Preserved five draft/revision endpoints and three numerical runs; inspected primary count, chronology and anchor observations; used shared-frame cells, block-level inference and adequacy denominators; separated archaeological survival from Indus attribution and operational feasibility. Two actual Claude Opus 5.5 reviews with tools disabled and commissioned Codex passes precede the final text. Successor registers resolve audit clarifications. Final source/output/export verification passes 41 checks, with 50 witnesses ignored and 69 complete PDF reference targets.
retry_when: Accessible reconciled project-level records and exact surveyed footprints, new local dates or preservation/detection calibration permit a new discriminating result. A named partner and verified access are required for field tasks. Do not repeat national artifact extrapolation, naive capture-recapture or site-size inference from geographic proximity using the same aggregate evidence.
